key_insight: Smaller reported uncertainty did not ensure accurate molecular energies: hardware bias and cross-job variability persisted, while mitigation improved some results at added cost.
engineering_relevance: Validate workloads with known-state controls and repeated runs before spending more QPU time on sampling or mitigation.
method: Evaluate noiselessly optimized molecular VQE states on IBM Aachen and Pittsburgh 156-qubit Heron processors.
Freeze parameters, layouts and compiled circuits; disable dynamical decoupling.
Compare raw evaluation, zero-noise extrapolation (ZNE) and twirled readout error extinction (TREX), alongside known-state controls.
evidence_signal: Across 110 jobs and 28.2 billed QPU minutes, Raw 1024 O2 and BeH2 mean residuals were 12–32 times returned uncertainty; ZNE reduced O2 absolute residuals by 49.7–83.5% at roughly fourfold charge.
watch_item: Mitigation requires physical-validity checks: 13 mitigated energy point estimates fell outside the mapped spectrum, versus none among raw estimates.
paper_title: Execution bias, repeatability and mitigation cost in parameter-frozen molecular VQE energy evaluation
